title: OpenAI Chat Completions compatibility gateway: deterministic stream reassembly and function-call fidelity
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: legacy clients relying on the OpenAI Chat Completions (CC) API expect deterministic SSE-style streaming chunks and exact function-call (tool) payloads. Our current compatibility layer occasionally produces different chunk boundaries, merges deltas differently, or normalizes tool-call arguments in ways that break idempotent client rehydration and downstream tool executors.

Background: Redwood must accept OA-CC requests and produce equivalent streaming responses (including function-call deltas) while also routing through our runtime optimizations (batching, caching, kernel shims). This ticket designs and implements a gateway that: (1) deterministically reassembles and emits SSE-style deltas so legacy clients see the same sequence on retries, (2) preserves function-call argument fidelity (order, types, whitespace, and nested JSON), and (3) adds telemetry/guards so we can safely roll out without regressing latency or reliability.

Goals:
- Make CC streaming behavior deterministic across retries and across our internal retries/hedging.
- Ensure function/tool-call objects are preserved exactly, including whitespace-sensitive strings and ordering inside arbitrary JSON arguments.
- Provide a graceful fallback to the existing compatibility behavior if the deterministic reassembler detects unresolvable gaps.
- Emit telemetry counters and histograms to detect reassembly failures and token-level truncation.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting model output semantics. We do not attempt to canonicalize AI-generated content beyond reassembly and faithful transport.
- Replacing the runtime batching engine; gateway must interoperate with it without introducing per-request throttles beyond a small reassembly buffer window.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy OA-CC client integration tests (provided) pass end-to-end for streaming completions and function calls without client-side changes
Deterministic reassembly verified: repeated replay of identical request + network reordering results in identical delta sequence (CI harness)
No more than +15ms median p50 added latency to end-to-end streaming path in canary (measurement window: 99th percentile remaining unchanged)
Function-call payloads are byte-preserved for JSON values where model intended literal strings or nested objects (tests cover 50+ real-world tool schemas)
Graceful fallback path engaged when missing/irrecoverable sequence frames detected; fallback causes an explicit compat-mode header so downstream telemetry can split traffic
Telemetry: emit reassembly_chunk_count, reassembly_time_ms, reassembly_error_code, fncall_truncation_flag; dashboards created before rollout
implementation_notes: Introduce a lightweight deterministic reassembly buffer at the CC gateway that sequences incoming stream frames by sequence_id + chunk_index (synthetic if missing) and emits ordered deltas to the client-facing SSE/HTTP stream

If upstream stream lacks stable seq ids, gateway will compute a hash(seq_origin, request_id, received_timestamp_floor) and attach monotonic chunk_index to reorder; this is recorded in telemetry (reassembly_mode: synthetic)

Preserve original byte payload for 'function_call' arguments: gateway must avoid naive JSON reserialization. Use a passthrough field raw_fn_args (base64) in the internal envelope and only surface human-readable json in debug endpoints
Add a short retey-dedup window (200ms default) for identical delta frames to handle duplicate upstream resends; identical is determined by content-hash, not timestamp
Backpressure: reassembly buffer bounded by total_bytes and total_chunks; when limits hit, emit a 'compat-fallback' marker to downstream and transition to permissive streaming with explicit header

Map OA finish_reason semantics to Redwood outcomes explicitly: map early_stop -> partial, length -> truncated, function_call -> function-invoked; preserve original finish_reason field on compat responses
Add a strict validation stage that compares reconstructed function_call JSON against canonical parsing rules; on mismatch log full raw payload + request id and set fncall_truncation_flag
Instrumentation: attach request_id, compat_gateway_version, reassembly_mode, chunk_count to every span and add a low-cardinality tag for fncall_preserved: true/false
test_plan: Unit: reassembler ordering tests with out-of-order, duplicate, and missing frames (target coverage 98%)
Integration: run legacy-client harness against canary gateway with synthetic network jitter and validate delta sequence equality
E2E: deploy canary to 5% of hosted API traffic, collect comparison diffs for 24h between legacy-compat and deterministic-compat modes
Chaos: introduce random chunk drop and delayed chunks between gateway and runtime to validate fallback behavior and no client hangs
Performance: run p50/p95/p99 latency bench with 10k concurrent streaming sessions; ensure CPU overhead per session < 40us on gateway service
rollout_plan: Feature-flag behind 'cc_deterministic_gateway' with three modes: off, synthetic-only, strict (strict requires upstream seq ids)
Start with synthetic-only in staging then canary: 5% traffic for 48h -> 20% for 72h -> 100% if no regressions
Monitor reassembly_error_code rate and fncall_truncation_flag; if fncall_truncation_flag > 0.05% for >1h, rollback to off for affected region
Expose a toggle in Console per-customer for Dedicated tenants to opt into strict mode after QA validation
Ship runbook that documents how to force-failover to legacy compatibility layer and how to collect reassembly artifacts for support escalation
comments: 2026-03-01 - Triage: identified multiple customer bug reports where legacy SDKs failed to parse fncall args when gateway reserialized JSON. Prioritized P0.
2026-03-03 - Spike complete: deterministic reassembly buffer adds ~9ms median overhead in devbench. Synthetic seq id approach able to reconstruct order in 98% of fuzz cases.

2026-03-05 - Architecture review: recommended preserving raw byte payload for function_call args to avoid semantic drift; security raised concerns about storing raw payloads in logs, we will base64 + redact in prod logs.
2026-03-09 - PR #1289 opened (initial reassembler + integration tests). Requesting review from @sre-team for backpressure behavior and @security for raw payload handling.
2026-03-12 - QA notes: one failing case around nested arrays where legacy client compared string keys; added unit test and fixed serializer bypass.
2026-03-14 - Ready for canary: feature flag implemented and console toggle in staging. Oncall runbook drafted; monitoring dashboards provisioned.
